decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1. The proposed redevelopment of this site in isolation from the land to the rear would prejudice the acceptable comprehensive redevelopment of this and adjoining sites, in particular due to the impact on privacy and obtrusiveness that this proposal would cause to the site to the rear on redevelopment. This would be contrary to Proposal M11, Policies IMP.2.1 and IMP.3.1 in the Council's Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001) and the adopted planning brief covering the site.

Condition : 2 - 2. The proposed residential development by reason of its height, bulk, massing and materials within close proximity to the River Thames would be detrimental to the appearance of the street scene and general locality and the setting of the River Thames. The excessive density with inadequate amenity space would be an overdevelopment of the site.  This would be contrary to Policies ENV.1.1, ENV.1.5 and ENV.6.1, H.1.2, H.1.4 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan and Policies ENV-B.1.1, ENV-B.1.2 and ENV-W.1.1, H.4.1, H.4.2 of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001).

Condition : 3 - 3. The proposal does not provide any affordable housing contrary to Policy H.4.1 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996) and Policy H.2.1 of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001)

Condition : 4 - 4. The loss of this essential isolated shop unit, which meets the day to day needs of local people and businesses, would be contrary to Policy S.1.3 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996) and Policy S.2.2 of the Revised Unitary Development Plan (2001).

Condition : 5 - 5. The proposal would lead to a significant loss of light and privacy to surrounding occupiers of residential properties contrary to Policies ENV.1.1 and H.1.2 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996) and Policies ENV-B.1.1 and H.4.1 of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001).

Condition : 6 - 6. The proposal fails to make adequate provision for educational provision arising from the development. This would be contrary to Policies H.1.7 and IMP.3.1 of the Council's Adopted Unitary Development Plan and Policies H.4.5 and IMP.6.1 of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001)

Condition : 7 - 7. The proposal has not been designed to create a safe and secure environment nor to reduce opportunities for crime and is therefore contrary to Policy ENV-B.1.9 of the Proposed Unitary Development Plan (2001) and Policy ENV.3.2 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996)

Condition : 8 - 8. The gradient of the access to the basement parking area, the lack of servicing, inadequate refuse arrangements and insufficient information regarding road markings, visibility splays and the relationship to other existing and proposed accesses and bus lanes. This would have a negative impact on highway and pedestrian safety and would therefore be contrary to Policy T.4.4 of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan (2001) and Policy T.3.6 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996).

Condition : 10 - 10. The proposal fails to provide a wheelchair accessible unit and does not make adequate provision for the disabled and others with mobility problems contrary to Policies ENV-B.1.8 and H.5.1 of the Proposed Unitary Development Plan (2001) and Policies ENV.3.1 and H.4.3 of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan (1996)

Condition : 11 - 11. It has not been demonstrated that the development can be carried out safely, without detriment to the development or adjoining land, on land which is known to be contaminated. It has not been demonstrated that the site is suitable for residential use. The proposal is thereby contrary to Policy ENV.P.1.8 of the Revised Deposit UDP (2001) and Policy ENV.7.2 of the Adopted UDP (1996).
description: Demolition of existing building and erection of a four storey building comprising 10 one bedroom apartments, 9 two bedroom apartments, and 3 three bedroom apartments with associated basement parking
